title: PACEE: Parent-Centered AI Scaffolding for Emotion Education in Early Childhood Conversations
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge of supporting emotion education for children aged 3 to 6, a period when children have limited verbalization and self-regulation skills and parents often lack practical guidance. The authors argue that most prior AI tools for emotional development target children directly, which is a poor fit for preschoolers and ignores the central role of parents in everyday emotion coaching at home.

To address this, the paper introduces PACEE, an LLM-based parent-centered scaffold for family emotion education. PACEE has three main modules: a real-time Parent-Child Conversational Scenario module that guides parents through Gottman’s five steps of emotion coaching, a Parental Feedback Report that summarizes and critiques parental guidance, and a Child Emotional Modeling module that builds a profile of the child’s emotional understanding, expression, and regulation from parent input and conversation analysis. The system is designed to support parents rather than replace them, and it includes trackable feedback so parents can reflect on what guidance was useful.

The study began with formative interviews with five kindergarten teachers and five parents, plus observations of five parent-child pairs, all in China. The evaluation then used a within-subject study with 16 parent-child pairs, comparing PACEE to a baseline voice-based LLM chatbot. Results suggest PACEE increased parent-child engagement, produced richer emotional dialogue, improved parents’ immediate experience and confidence, and helped parents reflect more deeply on their children’s emotional states. The authors conclude that AI can be effective as a reflective partner for parents in early childhood emotion coaching, but they also caution that the system is supportive rather than a validated measure of coaching skill.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: An LLM-based assistant that provides real-time conversational support, stage-aware guidance, scenario generation, actionable feedback, and child emotional profiling for parent-led early childhood emotion coaching.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as PACEE, a parent-centered AI scaffolding system to support parents in guiding children aged 3–6 through emotion-related conversations, compared against a generic voice-based LLM chatbot baseline (Doubao) with no PACEE features.

findings.finding_summary: In a within-subject study with 16 parent-child pairs, PACEE increased interaction duration (M=892.37s, SD=310.96) compared with the baseline LLM chatbot (M=560.17s, SD=194.61), with p<0.01. It also increased dialogue turns (M=60 vs. 38, p<0.05), parent word count (M=1597 vs. 994, p<0.05), child word count (M=370 vs. 165, p<0.001), and emotion-related word usage by both parents (M=111 vs. 70, p<0.05) and children (M=19 vs. 10, p<0.01).
findings.measure: Interaction duration, dialogue turns, word count, and emotion-related word usage during parent-child emotional conversations

findings.finding_summary: Parents reported better immediate interaction experience with PACEE than with the baseline, including higher satisfaction (M=5.06, SD=1.12 vs. 3.94, SD=1.57, p<0.05), lower effort (M=2.56, SD=1.79 vs. 3.62, SD=2.03, p<0.01), and reduced frustration (M=2.06, SD=1.24 vs. 3.06, SD=1.57, p<0.05). The paper notes that self-efficacy did not change significantly in this short study.
findings.measure: NASA-TLX and PSOC post-questionnaire ratings of interaction experience

findings.finding_summary: PACEE was rated as significantly better than the baseline in addressing the three family emotion-education challenges (limited parental expertise, insufficient feedback, and lack of understanding of children’s emotional states), each at p<0.01. Qualitatively, 14 of 16 parents found PACEE’s emotional-profile analysis useful as an external perspective, and parents reported adopting real-time suggestions such as collaborative problem-solving and open-ended questioning.
findings.measure: Post-questionnaire ratings and semi-structured parent interviews about system support for emotion coaching challenges

quality_tier_rationale: This is a single within-subject mixed-methods evaluation with qualitative interviews and non-randomized comparison to a baseline chatbot. It provides useful empirical evidence, but not the level of control or validation needed for a higher tier.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effects are practically meaningful in engagement and parent experience, but the paper does not report standardized effect sizes, and the study is short-term with no evidence of long-term coaching impact.
